name: VL53L4CD time-of-flight distance sensor
description: ST FlightSense short-range time-of-flight sensor that times 940 nm laser pulses to measure absolute distance from 1 mm up to about 1.3 m, read in millimetres over I2C (up to 1 MHz) at address 0x29 with 16-bit register addresses. The bare chip runs from 2.6–3.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit VL53L4CD Time of Flight Distance Sensor breakout (product 5396; 6-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, GPIO, XSHUT plus two STEMMA QT ports) with an LP5907 2.8 V regulator and level shifting, so VIN takes 3–5 V.
eli5: It flashes a tiny invisible laser and times how long the light takes to bounce back, which tells you how far away something is, from a millimetre up to about a metre.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply input, 3–5 V (on-board LP5907 regulator makes the chip's 2.8 V)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, level shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, level shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: GPIO
pins.description: Interrupt output (chip GPIO1), 2.8 V logic; signals a new range is ready (active low with the default settings)

pins.name: XSHUT

supplierQuery: Adafruit VL53L4CD time of flight distance sensor 5396
buildNotes: Peel off the protective film over the sensor window before use, or readings will be wrong.

Registers have 16-bit addresses: send the address MSB first, then data. The driver waits for boot (0x00E5 = 0x03), loads ST's 91-byte default configuration to 0x002D–0x0087, runs one VHV ranging and then ranges continuously (0x0087 = 0x21).
Each range is 16-bit mm at 0x0096; range status 0x0089 (low 5 bits) must be 9 for a valid reading. Write 0x01 to 0x0086 after every read or the result will not update.
Every VL53L4CD starts at address 0x29. For several on one bus hold their XSHUT pins low, release them one at a time and set a new address (register 0x0001).
Range is 1 mm to about 1.3 m indoors on a white target, about 0.55 m outdoors; use a VL53L1X for longer distances.
Ranging peaks at about 40 mA; keep power wires short or add a 10 µF capacitor near VIN.

driver.code:
# VL53L4CD time-of-flight distance sensor (ST), MicroPython driver.
# Follows ST's Ultra Lite Driver (ULD, STSW-IMG026, as published in stm32duino/VL53L4CD):
# 16-bit register addresses, wait for FIRMWARE__SYSTEM_STATUS = 3, load the 91-byte default
# configuration to 0x2D..0x87, one VHV ranging, then ranging started through SYSTEM_START
# (0x21 = continuous back-to-back, 0x40 = autonomous with an inter-measurement period).
import time

_I2C_SLAVE_DEVICE_ADDRESS = 0x0001
_OSC_FREQUENCY = 0x0006                      # 16-bit, read by SetRangeTiming
_VHV_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_LOOP_BOUND = 0x0008
_RANGE_OFFSET_MM = 0x001E
_INNER_OFFSET_MM = 0x0020
_OUTER_OFFSET_MM = 0x0022
_GPIO_HV_MUX_CTRL = 0x0030
_GPIO_TIO_HV_STATUS = 0x0031
_RANGE_CONFIG_A = 0x005E
_RANGE_CONFIG_B = 0x0061
_INTERMEASUREMENT_MS = 0x006C                # 32-bit
_SYSTEM_INTERRUPT_CLEAR = 0x0086
_SYSTEM_START = 0x0087
_RESULT_RANGE_STATUS = 0x0089
_RESULT_SPAD_NB = 0x008C                     # 16-bit, number of SPADs x 256
_RESULT_SIGNAL_RATE = 0x008E                 # 16-bit, kcps / 8
_RESULT_AMBIENT_RATE = 0x0090                # 16-bit, kcps / 8
_RESULT_SIGMA = 0x0092                       # 16-bit, mm x 4
_RESULT_DISTANCE = 0x0096                    # 16-bit, mm
_RESULT_OSC_CALIBRATE_VAL = 0x00DE
_FIRMWARE_SYSTEM_STATUS = 0x00E5
_IDENTIFICATION_MODEL_ID = 0x010F            # 0xEB, then module type 0xAA at 0x0110

# ST ULD default configuration for registers 0x2D..0x87 (91 bytes).
_DEFAULT_CONFIG = bytes((
    0x12, 0x00, 0x00, 0x11, 0x02, 0x00, 0x02, 0x08,  # 0x2D..0x34
    0x00, 0x08, 0x10, 0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x35..0x3C
    0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x0F, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x3D..0x44
    0x00, 0x20, 0x0B, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 0x14, 0x21,  # 0x45..0x4C
    0x00, 0x00, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xC8,  # 0x4D..0x54
    0x00, 0x00, 0x38, 0xFF, 0x01, 0x00, 0x08, 0x00,  # 0x55..0x5C
    0x00, 0x01, 0xCC, 0x07, 0x01, 0xF1, 0x05, 0x00,  # 0x5D..0x64
    0xA0, 0x00, 0x80, 0x08, 0x38, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x65..0x6C
    0x00, 0x0F, 0x89, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x6D..0x74
    0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x07, 0x05, 0x06, 0x06, 0x00,  # 0x75..0x7C
    0x00, 0x02, 0xC7, 0xFF, 0x9B, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,  # 0x7D..0x84
    0x01, 0x00, 0x00,                                # 0x85..0x87
))

# RESULT__RANGE_STATUS (low 5 bits) -> ULD range status (0 = valid), from VL53L4CD_GetResult.
_STATUS = (255, 255, 255, 5, 2, 4, 1, 7, 3, 0, 255, 255, 9, 13, 255, 255,
           255, 255, 10, 6, 255, 255, 11, 12)

_M32 = 0xFFFFFFFF


class VL53L4CD:
    def __init__(self, i2c, address=0x29, io_2v8=True, timeout_ms=1000):
        """io_2v8=True when SDA/SCL/GPIO1 are pulled up to the 2.8 V AVDD (Adafruit 5396,
        Pololu, SATEL boards). Use False only for a bare chip on a 1.8 V I/O bus."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = address
        self.timeout_ms = timeout_ms
        self.range_status = 255
        self.sigma_mm = 0
        self.signal_kcps = 0
        mid = self._rd(_IDENTIFICATION_MODEL_ID, 2)
        if mid[0] != 0xEB or mid[1] != 0xAA:
            raise OSError('VL53L4CD not found (model id %02X%02X, expected EBAA)' % (mid[0], mid[1]))
        # ULD SensorInit
        self._wait(lambda: self._rd(_FIRMWARE_SYSTEM_STATUS, 1)[0] == 0x03, 'boot')
        cfg = bytearray(_DEFAULT_CONFIG)
        if io_2v8:
            cfg[0x2E - 0x2D] |= 0x01  # I2C pads pulled up at AVDD
            cfg[0x2F - 0x2D] |= 0x01  # GPIO pad pulled up at AVDD
        self._wr(0x2D, cfg)
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_START, b'\x40')          # start VHV
        self._wait(self.data_ready, 'VHV')
        self.clear_interrupt()
        self.stop_ranging()
        self._wr(_VHV_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MACROP_LOOP_BOUND, b'\x09')
        self._wr(0x000B, b'\x00')
        self._wr16(0x0024, 0x0500)
        self.set_range_timing(50, 0)

    # ---- low level: 16-bit register addresses, big-endian data ----
    def _wr(self, reg, data):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes(((reg >> 8) & 0xFF, reg & 0xFF)) + bytes(data))

    def _rd(self, reg, n):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes(((reg >> 8) & 0xFF, reg & 0xFF)))
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    def _wr16(self, reg, v):
        self._wr(reg, bytes(((v >> 8) & 0xFF, v & 0xFF)))

    def _wr32(self, reg, v):
        self._wr(reg, bytes(((v >> 24) & 0xFF, (v >> 16) & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF, v & 0xFF)))

    def _rd16(self, reg):
        d = self._rd(reg, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def _rd32(self, reg):
        d = self._rd(reg, 4)
        return (d[0] << 24) | (d[1] << 16) | (d[2] << 8) | d[3]

    def _wait(self, cond, what):
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while not cond():
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > self.timeout_ms:
                raise OSError('VL53L4CD timeout waiting for ' + what)
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    # ---- ranging control ----
    def data_ready(self):
        # GPIO_HV_MUX_CTRL bit 4 = 1 means the interrupt is active low (the default config).
        pol = 0 if self._rd(_GPIO_HV_MUX_CTRL, 1)[0] & 0x10 else 1
        return (self._rd(_GPIO_TIO_HV_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x01) == pol

    def clear_interrupt(self):
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_INTERRUPT_CLEAR, b'\x01')

    def start_ranging(self):
        if self._rd32(_INTERMEASUREMENT_MS) == 0:
            self._wr(_SYSTEM_START, b'\x21')      # continuous, back-to-back
        else:
            self._wr(_SYSTEM_START, b'\x40')      # autonomous, timed
        self._wait(self.data_ready, 'first range')
        self.clear_interrupt()

    def stop_ranging(self):
        self._wr(_SYSTEM_START, b'\x00')

    # ---- settings ----
    def set_range_timing(self, timing_budget_ms, inter_measurement_ms=0):
        """Timing budget 10..200 ms. inter_measurement_ms = 0 ranges back to back (continuous);
        otherwise it must be larger than the timing budget (autonomous low-power mode)."""
        osc = self._rd16(_OSC_FREQUENCY)
        if osc == 0:
            raise OSError('VL53L4CD oscillator frequency reads 0')
        if not 10 <= timing_budget_ms <= 200:
            raise ValueError('timing budget must be 10..200 ms')
        macro_period_us = ((2304 * (0x40000000 // osc)) & _M32) >> 6
        tb_us = timing_budget_ms * 1000
        if inter_measurement_ms == 0:
            self._wr32(_INTERMEASUREMENT_MS, 0)
            tb_us -= 2500
        elif inter_measurement_ms > timing_budget_ms:
            clock_pll = self._rd16(_RESULT_OSC_CALIBRATE_VAL) & 0x3FF
            self._wr32(_INTERMEASUREMENT_MS, int(1.055 * inter_measurement_ms * clock_pll) & _M32)
            tb_us -= 4300
            tb_us //= 2
        else:
            raise ValueError('inter-measurement period must be 0 or longer than the timing budget')
        tb_us = (tb_us << 12) & _M32
        for reg, mult in ((_RANGE_CONFIG_A, 16), (_RANGE_CONFIG_B, 12)):
            t = ((macro_period_us * mult) & _M32) >> 6
            ls = (tb_us + (t >> 1)) // t - 1
            ms = 0
            while ls & 0xFFFFFF00:
                ls >>= 1
                ms += 1
            self._wr16(reg, (ms << 8) + (ls & 0xFF))
        self._tb = timing_budget_ms

    def set_offset(self, offset_mm):
        """Offset correction in mm (from ST's offset calibration flow)."""
        self._wr16(_RANGE_OFFSET_MM, (offset_mm * 4) & 0xFFFF)
        self._wr16(_INNER_OFFSET_MM, 0)
        self._wr16(_OUTER_OFFSET_MM, 0)

    def set_address(self, new_addr):
        """new_addr is the 7-bit address (the ULD takes the 8-bit form and shifts it)."""
        self._wr(_I2C_SLAVE_DEVICE_ADDRESS, bytes((new_addr & 0x7F,)))
        self.addr = new_addr

    # ---- measurement ----
    def read(self):
        """Wait for the next range. Returns the distance in mm, or None if the range status
        is not valid (no target, signal too weak, out of range). Call start_ranging() first."""
        self._wait(self.data_ready, 'data')
        raw = self._rd(_RESULT_RANGE_STATUS, 1)[0] & 0x1F
        st = _STATUS[raw] if raw < 24 else raw
        spads = self._rd16(_RESULT_SPAD_NB) // 256
        if spads == 0:
            st = 255
            mm = 0
        else:
            self.signal_kcps = self._rd16(_RESULT_SIGNAL_RATE) * 8
            self.sigma_mm = self._rd16(_RESULT_SIGMA) // 4
            mm = self._rd16(_RESULT_DISTANCE)
        self.clear_interrupt()
        self.range_status = st
        return mm if st == 0 else None

# VL53L4CD time-of-flight distance sensor (VL53L4CD)

## Overview
The **VL53L4CD** from STMicroelectronics is a FlightSense time-of-flight sensor for short distances. It fires 940 nm infrared laser pulses (Class 1, eye-safe) and times the reflections, giving an absolute distance in millimetres from **1 mm up to about 1.3 m** (white target, indoors). It is a short-range relative of the VL53L1X with better accuracy close up.
- Max range with a 33 ms timing budget: about 1200 mm (white, indoors), 450 mm (grey 17 %), about 550 mm outdoors (overcast).
- Linear response from 1 mm; field of view 18°.
- Timing budget 10–200 ms; back-to-back (continuous) or autonomous low-power mode with an inter-measurement period.
- Modelled board: **Adafruit VL53L4CD Time of Flight Distance Sensor (product 5396)**. It has an LP5907 2.8 V regulator, BSS138 level shifting on SDA/SCL/XSHUT, 10 kΩ pull-ups, a green power LED and two STEMMA QT connectors.

## Pinout (Adafruit 5396, header order)
| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| VIN | Supply, 3–5 V (regulated to 2.8 V on the board) |
| GND | Ground |
| SCL | I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up, level shifted) |
| SDA | I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up, level shifted) |
| GPIO | Interrupt output (GPIO1), 2.8 V logic, data ready (active low by default) |
| XSHUT | Shutdown input, active low, level shifted |

## Electrical limits
- Bare chip AVDD: 2.6–3.5 V (typ. 2.8 V). Never put more than 3.5 V on a bare module; the Adafruit board's regulator takes 3–5 V on VIN.
- Current: 22 mA typical, 24 mA max while ranging (average); peaks up to 40 mA. HW standby (XSHUT low) about 5 µA.
- I2C up to 1 MHz (Fast mode plus). Boot takes up to 1.2 ms after XSHUT goes high.

## Interface details
- **I2C address 0x29** (7-bit; the datasheet gives the 8-bit form 0x52). Change it in software through register 0x0001; it resets on power-up or XSHUT.
- **16-bit register addresses**, sent MSB first; multi-byte data is big-endian.
- ID: 0x010F = **0xEB** (model ID), 0x0110 = **0xAA** (module type).
- Init (ST Ultra Lite Driver, STSW-IMG026): wait for 0x00E5 = 0x03 (booted), write the 91-byte default configuration to 0x002D–0x0087, start VHV (0x0087 = 0x40), wait for data ready, clear the interrupt (0x0086 = 0x01), stop (0x0087 = 0x00), then 0x0008 = 0x09, 0x000B = 0x00, 0x0024 = 0x0500 and set the range timing (50 ms).
- Start ranging: 0x0087 = 0x21 when the inter-measurement period (0x006C, 32-bit) is 0, else 0x40. Stop: 0x0087 = 0x00.
- Data ready: 0x0031 bit 0 equals the interrupt polarity. The default config sets 0x0030 bit 4, so the interrupt is **active low** and data is ready when bit 0 reads 0.
- Result: 0x0096–0x0097 = distance in **mm** (16-bit unsigned). 0x0089 bits 4:0 = range status (9 = valid); 0x008C = SPAD count × 256 (0 means no result); 0x0092 = sigma × 4 mm; 0x008E = signal rate / 8 kcps.
- After each reading write 0x01 to 0x0086, or the next result does not arrive.
- ST publishes no full register map; the driver follows the ULD source exactly.

## Wiring
| Breakout | ESP32 | Raspberry Pi Pico | Raspberry Pi 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| VIN | 3V3 | 3V3(OUT) pin 36 | 3.3 V pin 1 |
| GND | GND | GND pin 38 | GND pin 6 |
| SDA | GPIO21 | GP4 (pin 6) | GPIO2 SDA pin 3 |
| SCL | GPIO22 | GP5 (pin 7) | GPIO3 SCL pin 5 |
| XSHUT | optional GPIO | optional GPIO | optional GPIO |
| GPIO | optional GPIO (IRQ) | optional GPIO | optional GPIO |

On a Raspberry Pi 4 running Linux use `adafruit-circuitpython-vl53l4cd` instead of this MicroPython driver.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from vl53l4cd import VL53L4CD

i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(4), scl=Pin(5), freq=400000)   # Pico
tof = VL53L4CD(i2c)          # 50 ms timing budget, continuous
tof.start_ranging()
while True:
    mm = tof.read()           # None when the range status is not valid
    print('out of range' if mm is None else 'D=%d mm' % mm)
    time.sleep_ms(200)
```
`tof.set_range_timing(100, 0)` (call before `start_ranging()`) trades speed for repeatability; `tof.set_range_timing(50, 200)` ranges every 200 ms in low-power autonomous mode. `tof.range_status` holds the last ULD status (0 = valid, 1 = sigma above threshold, 2 = signal too low, 3 = below detection threshold, 4 = phase out of limits, 7 = wrap-around, 255 = no result); `tof.sigma_mm` and `tof.signal_kcps` hold the quality figures.

**Several sensors on one bus:** hold every XSHUT low, release one, create `VL53L4CD(i2c)` and call `set_address(0x30)`, then release the next and give it another address.

## Gotchas
- **Peel off the protective film** over the sensor window first.
- Maximum range is only about 1.3 m; for longer distances use a VL53L1X.
- Sunlight and other IR shorten range (about 0.55 m outdoors); a cover glass needs ST's offset/crosstalk calibration (`set_offset`).
- The address returns to 0x29 at every power cycle or XSHUT reset.
- The driver uses `writeto`/`readfrom` with a two-byte register address, so it works on MicroPython ports whose `readfrom_mem` lacks `addrsize=16`.

## Datasheet
https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/vl53l4cd.pdf (DS13812; mirror used: https://cdn-learn.adafruit.com/assets/assets/000/109/710/original/vl53l4cd.pdf)
